summary:
1. Focus exclusively on direct bodily phenomena and visceral human experiences rather than cold engineering or niche environmental topics.
2. Keep opening sentences under 12 words and deliver an immediate myth-bust or startling statement in present tense using second-person ('Your...').
3. Eliminate scenario roleplay setups ('You swerve off...') and rhetorical openings ('Ever noticed...'), which plummet stayed_pct below 37%.
4. Keep video duration strictly under 25 seconds, as longer videos (30-50s) suffer heavy viewer drop-off and fail to reach the 1,200 view threshold.
5. Write titles using visceral, active phrasing ('Eat You Back', 'Secretly Leaking') rather than descriptive academic summaries.
winning_hooks: Present-tense body horror/curiosity: 'Your eyes are leaking right now, and your brain is hiding it.' (stayed_pct: 51.9%)
Direct punchy myth-buster: 'Your fingers prune in water, but it is not because you are absorbing it like a sponge.' (stayed_pct: 65.6%)
Visceral anthropomorphism (<8 words): 'Fresh pineapple is literally eating you back.' (stayed_pct: 57.6%)
Extreme relatable baseline contrast: 'This shark is older than the United States.' (stayed_pct: 56.2%)
avoid: Rhetorical question openings: 'Ever noticed those tiny black dots fading around your car windshield?' (stayed_pct: 36.8%)
Fictional roleplay/narrative scenarios: 'Your car swerves off the highway right toward a steel guardrail.' (stayed_pct: 30.4%)
Wordy academic explanations: 'Massive acorn drops trigger Lyme disease spikes two years later...' (stayed_pct: 44.7%, views: 47)
Contradictory/Confusing setup statements: 'Drop an apple or a pear in a bowl of water and they both float.' (stayed_pct: 27.2%)
Longer durations (30-50 seconds): All videos in this length band failed to reach 600 views.
next_experiment: A/B test a 20-second body-science topic with Hook A (Direct Myth-Bust: 'Your stomach isn't digesting food the way you think it is.') vs Hook B (Visceral Statement: 'Your stomach acid is strong enough to dissolve metal right now.'). Measure stayed_pct against the 55% threshold.
